content_list.content_text: With the disenchantment of the late 1960s and early 1970s, cinema tended to scorn the thrills of chases, cowboy movies or secret agent films. Bullitt (1968) and The French Connection (1971) may have offered elaborate car chases, but their context involved cynicism, political scheming and heroes who challenged the system.

information.contentText: Desperate for work, Stuart was offered the job of adapting Thorp's novel into a screenplay. His final draft was immediately green-lit by 20th Century Fox, which was eager for a summer blockbuster for the following year. Finding a star was difficult: the role of McClane was offered to a string of the decade's biggest stars, including Arnold Schwarzenegger and Sylvester Stallone, who turned it down. Willis, who was known mainly for his TV work, was eventually cast and paid $5 million for the role, an unprecedented sum at the time that stirred considerable controversy around the film before its release.

content_list.content_text: Dirty Harry (1971) turned cowboy Clint Eastwood (b. 1930) into Harry Callahan, the archetypal cop of urban action films. Traditional Westerns and war films were replaced by sermons on the evils of violence, graphically presented in films by Sam Peckinpah (1925-1984) such as The Wild Bunch (1969) and Straw Dogs (1971).

quote.quote: An army which carries the Ark before it... is invincible.
quote.author: Dr. Marcus Brody (Denholm Elliott) in Raiders of the Lost Ark

content_list.content_text: Martial arts action films made an explosive entrance with mainstream Western audiences in the early 1970s, thanks to the iconic Bruce Lee (1940-1973). Enter the Dragon (1973) was the first Chinese martial arts film produced by a major Hollywood studio. Although Lee did not live to see the final result, his work influenced martial arts films around the world for many decades.

information.contentTitle: Scenes from Raiders of the Lost Ark
information.contentText: The screenplay was written by Lawrence Kasdan, after a four-day discussion in which he, Spielberg and Lucas defined the main narrative elements of the plot. The film's conception originated when Lucas decided to create a modern version of the serials of the 1930s and 1940s. Production took place at Elstree Studios in England, but shooting also took place in La Rochelle, Tunisia, Hawaii and California from June to September 1980.

content_list.content_text: By the late 1970s, the climate had changed again. Directed by George Lucas (b. 1944), Star Wars (1977) is a return to the comic-strip era of the 1930s, with heroes like Flash Gordon, in which space battles are antiseptic - planets are blown up without any real sense of suffering - and bombings, a massacre at a farm and sword duels are not felt episodes but references to scenes from earlier films. Lucas and his friend Steven Spielberg (b. 1946) continued to show their love for old-fashioned adventure with Raiders of the Lost Ark (1981).

content_list.title: The Science Fiction Landmark in Cinema
content_list.description:
This potential contender for a Golden Turkey Award in the "kitsch" category ended up becoming one of the big hits of 1984, and its enduring popularity has enshrined it as a classic of the genre. The Terminator is a triumph of style over plot, of cleverness over intelligence, and a combination of elements that adds up to more than the sum of its parts. Its circular narrative about the future's attempt to control the past in order to take control of itself, thereby changing the premises of its own state, is familiar to every fan of postwar science fiction literature (Harlan Ellison, Philip K. Dick, and others) and of postwar television series (such as The Outer Limits and Star Trek).

Shortly after completing low-budget special effects for Roger Corman (b. 1926) and John Carpenter (b. 1948), writer-director James Cameron (b. 1954) adopted his mentors' disarming humor to shield himself from objections about the many plot holes. The vision of a bleak, dark, apocalyptic future was fashionable at the time, as attested by Escape from New York (1981), by John Carpenter, Mad Max (1979), by George Miller (b. 1945), Le dernier combat (The Last Battle, 1983), by Luc Besson (b. 1959), and Forbrydelsens Element (The Element of Crime, 1984), by Lars von Trier (b. 1956).

Cameron's assured style (tech noir, as it was called after a nightclub in the film) and his kinetic energy combined with narrative economy keep the viewer distracted from the absurdity of the whole thing. Even Arnold Schwarzenegger, the epitome of bad acting with his cold facial expression, heavy Austrian accent, and body language learned at the same school as Frankenstein's monster, becomes a major triumph for the film. The casting, Cameron admitted to Wired magazine, "shouldn't have worked. The guy is supposed to be an infiltrator, and it's impossible not to spot him immediately in a crowd, unless everyone looked like Arnold". Nevertheless, everyone who has seen this unlikely phenomenon knows most of the film's lines by heart, including Schwarzenegger's peculiar pronunciation. "I'll be back" is probably the most quoted line of all, often used as a catchphrase on radio and television shows.

If The Terminator's ability to engage its audience recalls the fan cult of The Rocky Horror Picture Show (1975), its insistent irony points ahead to the jokes of the Scream series (1999-2011), built on generic clichés. The same can be said of the sadistic violence and the heroine's turnaround at the end. Beneath the surface of this cut-and-paste of science fiction elements lies an even less original slasher movie, featuring a (literally) mechanical killer and a tough heroine (Linda Hamilton) who discovers her capacity to fight back and combat evil. The film's appeal, as with all great films, does not come from its supposed originality. It is the way Cameron brings together familiar elements and breathes new life into them that results in such a memorable experience, one that ultimately changed science fiction films in theaters forever.
content_list.credits: Summary based on the text by Michael Tapper, published in the book 1001 Movies You Must See Before You Die.

content_list.content_text: Directed by Richard Donner (b. 1930), Superman (1978) made audiences "believe a man can fly" - and that Clark Kent (Christopher Reeve) was not an outdated character. Alex Raymond's comic-strip hero also got a reinterpretation in Flash Gordon (1980), but despite its camp style and Queen soundtrack, the film did poorly at the box office. Batman (1989), by Tim Burton (b. 1958), was more successful in 1989, offering a darker, more gothic superhero in the introspective Bruce Wayne (Michael Keaton).

information.contentText: Schwarzenegger tried to change the iconic line "I'll be back," as he had difficulty pronouncing the word "back." He also felt that his robotic character would not speak in contractions and that the Terminator would be more declarative. Cameron refused to change the line to "I will be back," so Schwarzenegger worked to deliver the line as written as best he could. He would later say the line in several films throughout his career.

content_list.content_text: In the 1980s, action and adventure films featured ever more muscular heroes. Arnold Schwarzenegger (b. 1947) flexed his pecs and grunted a few words as Conan in Conan the Barbarian (1982) and as the Terminator in The Terminator (1984). Sylvester Stallone (b. 1946) turned Rambo in First Blood (1982) from a traumatized Vietnam veteran at war with his own country into a superhero ready to settle the score ("Do we get to win this time?"), and Rocky from a washed-up bulldog into a champion of the United States.

quote.quote: Nine million terrorists in the world and I gotta kill one with feet smaller than my sister.
quote.author: John McClane (Bruce Willis) in Die Hard

content_list.content_text: Bruce Willis (b. 1955), then best known as Cybill Shepherd's (b. 1950) irreverent partner on the TV series Moonlighting, took on fake terrorists in a one-man crusade in Die Hard (1988) and its popular sequels. These films were full of montages in which macho men work out their bodies, displaying a sweaty perfection, or gather a ridiculous number of firearms in a scene of gun fetishism.

information.contentText: The original screenplay for "First Blood" called for John Rambo, at the end of the film, to commit suicide after talking with Colonel Samuel Trautman. The scene was actually shot, but it was cut from the film, and a new ending, with John Rambo being arrested, was filmed.

content_list.content_text: Commando (1985) is perhaps the most delirious and sado-erotic of these spectacles of brutes taking on brutes, but Predator (1987) comes a close second, pitting Arnie against an alien. Dip huet seung hung (The Killer, 1989), by Hong Kong filmmaker John Woo (b. 1946), inspired a series of similar (and violent) films, such as Léon: The Professional (1994). Meanwhile, Lethal Weapon (1987), with Mel Gibson (b. 1956) and Danny Glover (b. 1946), was just one of many mismatched cop pairings in buddy cop movies, such as Stakeout (1987).

The Bond franchise returned with Timothy Dalton (b. 1946) in two more violent installments that foreshadowed later entries with Pierce Brosnan (b. 1953) and Daniel Craig (b. 1956). Meanwhile, in Aliens (1986), James Cameron (b. 1954) followed up Alien (1979) with more straight-ahead action than horror - "This time it's war" - and with Sigourney Weaver (b. 1959) returning as the tough, independent Ellen Ripley.
content_list.content_credits: Summary based on the text by Kim Newman, published in the book "Cinema: The Whole Story" by Philip Kemp.

movies.title: The Terminator
movies.overview: In the post-apocalyptic future, reigning tyrannical supercomputers teleport a cyborg assassin known as the "Terminator" back to 1984 to kill Sarah Connor, whose unborn son is destined to lead insurgents against 21st century mechanical hegemony. Meanwhile, the human-resistance movement dispatches a lone warrior to safeguard Sarah. Can he stop the virtually indestructible killing machine?

movies.title: Raiders of the Lost Ark
movies.overview: When Dr. Indiana Jones – the tweed-suited professor who just happens to be a celebrated archaeologist – is hired by the government to locate the legendary Ark of the Covenant, he finds himself up against the entire Nazi regime.

movies.title: Die Hard
movies.overview: NYPD cop John McClane's plan to reconcile with his estranged wife is thrown for a serious loop when, minutes after he arrives at her office, the entire building is overtaken by a group of terrorists. With little help from the LAPD, wisecracking McClane sets out to single-handedly rescue the hostages and bring the bad guys down.

movies.title: Aliens
movies.overview: When Ripley's lifepod is found by a salvage crew over 50 years later, she finds that terra-formers are on the very planet they found the alien species. When the company sends a family of colonists out to investigate her story—all contact is lost with the planet and colonists. They enlist Ripley and the colonial marines to return and search for answers.

movies.name: Lethal Weapon
movies.overview: A slightly unhinged former Navy SEAL lands a job as a police officer in Los Angeles where he's partnered with a veteran detective trying to keep maintain a low stress level in his life.

movies.title: Enter the Dragon
movies.overview: A martial artist agrees to spy on a reclusive crime lord using his invitation to a tournament there as cover.

movies.title: Dirty Harry
movies.overview: When a madman dubbed 'Scorpio' terrorizes San Francisco, hard-nosed cop, Harry Callahan – famous for his take-no-prisoners approach to law enforcement – is tasked with hunting down the psychopath. Harry eventually collars Scorpio in the process of rescuing a kidnap victim, only to see him walk on technicalities. Now, the maverick detective is determined to nail the maniac himself.

movies.title: Star Wars
movies.overview: Princess Leia is captured and held hostage by the evil Imperial forces in their effort to take over the galactic Empire. Venturesome Luke Skywalker and dashing captain Han Solo team together with the loveable robot duo R2-D2 and C-3PO to rescue the beautiful princess and restore peace and justice in the Empire.

movies.title: Superman
movies.overview: Mild-mannered Clark Kent works as a reporter at the Daily Planet alongside his crush, Lois Lane. Clark must summon his superhero alter-ego when the nefarious Lex Luthor launches a plan to take over the world.

movies.title: Batman
movies.overview: Having witnessed his parents' brutal murder as a child, millionaire philanthropist Bruce Wayne fights crime in Gotham City disguised as Batman, a costumed hero who strikes fear into the hearts of villains. But when a deformed madman who calls himself "The Joker" seizes control of Gotham's criminal underworld, Batman must face his most ruthless nemesis ever while protecting both his identity and his love interest, reporter Vicki Vale.

movies.title: Missing in Action
movies.overview: American servicemen are still being held captive in Vietnam and it's up to one man to bring them home in this blistering, fast-paced action/adventure starring martial arts superstar Chuck Norris.Following a daring escape from a Vietnamese POW camp, Special Forces Colonel James Braddock (Norris) is on a mission to locate and save remaining MIAs.

movies.title: Conan the Destroyer
movies.overview: Conan is commissioned by the evil queen Taramis to safely escort a teen princess and her powerful bodyguard to a far away castle to retrieve the magic Horn of Dagon. Unknown to Conan, the queen plans to sacrifice the princess when she returns and inherit her kingdom after the bodyguard kills Conan. The queen's plans fail to take into consideration Conan's strength and cunning and the abilities of his sidekicks: the eccentric wizard Akiro, the wild woman Zula, and the inept Malak. Together the hero and his allies must defeat both mortal and supernatural foes in this voyage to sword-and-sorcery land.

movies.title: First Blood
movies.overview: When former Green Beret John Rambo is harassed by local law enforcement and arrested for vagrancy, the Vietnam vet snaps, runs for the hills and rat-a-tat-tats his way into the action-movie hall of fame. Hounded by a relentless sheriff, Rambo employs heavy-handed guerilla tactics to shake the cops off his tail.

movies.title: Commando
movies.overview: John Matrix, the former leader of a special commando strike force that always got the toughest jobs done, is forced back into action when his young daughter is kidnapped. To find her, Matrix has to fight his way through an array of punks, killers, one of his former commandos, and a fully equipped private army. With the help of a feisty stewardess and an old friend, Matrix has only a few hours to overcome his greatest challenge: finding his daughter before she's killed.

movies.title: Bloodsport
movies.overview: U.S. soldier Frank Dux has come to Hong Kong to be accepted into the Kumite, a highly secret and extremely violent martial arts competition. While trying to gain access into the underground world of clandestine fighters, he also has to avoid military officers who consider him to be AWOL. After enduring a difficult training and beginning a romance with journalist Janice Kent, Frank is given the opportunity to fight. But can he survive?

movies.title: A Force of One
movies.overview: Karate champion Matt Logan is enlisted by the police to train officers in self-defense after narcotics agents are killed by an assailant using the martial arts.

movies.title: The Living Daylights
movies.overview: James Bond helps a Russian General escape into the west. He soon finds out that the KGB wants to kill him for helping the General. A little while later the General is kidnapped from the Secret Service leading 007 to be suspicious.

movies.title: La Femme Nikita
movies.overview: A beautiful felon, sentenced to life in prison for the murder of a policeman, is given a second chance - as a secret political assassin controlled by the government.

content_list.subtitle: The events that shaped the world
content_list.title: Timeline of Events from 1970 to 1989
content_list.description: The Exorcist is released, making audiences around the world sick and causing them to faint, creating a global hysteria. The first blockbuster is released: Jaws; meanwhile, auteur cinema grows with Martin Scorsese and other great directors. The '80s arrive with low-budget productions and era-defining comedies. Click here to see, in chronological order, the main events in cinema between 1940 and 1959.
